# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

payload.rationale: I covered the anti-real-time-chat and decision-capture narratives and positions because the ruling explicitly contrasts reader-facing bundled delivery with per-skill messages, and I included the context-preservation thread as a related question of keeping decisions and their producing context together. I also surfaced the zero-effort capture narrative, webhook and integration positions, the Sprint 4 thesis position, and the batching-related rate-limit observation because they provide the closest existing delivery and batching context. The thematic and documents doors revealed no separate delivery-routing node, and the people door was unavailable; I left unrelated pricing and target-market threads unexpanded.
